metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the share of provisioned compute doing real work over time, not at peak, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.

Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. In most enterprise estates, fleet utilization is where the money hides, so a low rate means paying for compute that never runs a workload. That wasted power is real consumption with no corresponding output.

The metric does not say whether the work is valuable, only that servers are doing real work. It also does not explain why utilization is low, whether from overprovisioning, poor scheduling, or stranded capacity. It is one of several capacity and server use measures, alongside stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits.
